title: Programmable Coherent Memory Kernels for Quantum Reservoir Computing in Waveguide QED
authors: Hong Jiang, Yu Wu, Yue Ban, Xi Chen, Juan José García-Ripoll
abstract: Reservoir computing requires not only long memory, but also memory distributed over the timescales relevant to a given task. In most quantum reservoir computing architectures, however, the memory profile emerges from intrinsic dynamics and cannot be directly engineered. Here we introduce a waveguide-QED quantum reservoir in which coherent memory return is controlled by the coupling geometry. The reservoir consists of a driven Kerr-nonlinear resonator coupled to a one-dimensional waveguide at spatially separated points. An unmeasured propagating field carries information about past inputs and coherently returns it to the resonator after a finite propagation time, forming a non-Markovian feedback channel without intermediate measurement or classical reinjection. Delay-resolved memory benchmarks reveal two complementary functions: waveguide propagation determines when past information returns, whereas Kerr dynamics convert the returned field into nonlinear temporal features accessible through a linear readout. NARMA-$n$ prediction shows that the optimal feedback delay shifts systematically with task order and approximately tracks the explicit input-product lag. These results establish coherent delayed feedback as a mechanism for engineering task-relevant memory in quantum reservoir computing.
summary: This paper proposes using a waveguide-QED system to create a quantum reservoir with programmable memory. By coupling a nonlinear resonator to a waveguide, the system achieves coherent, delayed feedback that acts as a controllable memory source. This establishes a novel physical mechanism for engineering memory required for advanced quantum machine learning tasks.
main_problem: The core challenge is engineering task-relevant memory profiles in Quantum Reservoir Computing (QRC) because intrinsic dynamics do not naturally provide the necessary memory control.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that coherent delayed feedback, realized via a waveguide-QED setup, provides a hardware-level mechanism to engineer task-relevant memory in QRC.
method: The study models the reservoir using a driven Kerr-nonlinear resonator coupled nonlocally to a 1D waveguide, deriving the memory kernel from the waveguide propagation delay.
model_or_system: The physical system is a waveguide-QED quantum reservoir, involving a Kerr-nonlinear resonator coupled to a 1D waveguide. The dynamics are governed by a Hamiltonian incorporating Kerr nonlinearity and coupling terms, leading to a non-Markovian feedback channel.
key_observables: Delay-resolved memory benchmarks, including Short-Term-Memory (STM) capacity ($C_{	ext{STM}}^d$) and delayed-product capacity ($C_{	ext{prod}}^d$), and the prediction error (NRMSE) for time-series forecasting.

main_assumptions: The method assumes that the unmeasured propagating field acts as a coherent memory carrier, avoiding intermediate measurement or classical reinjection.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the waveguide-QED setup, showing how the resonator response depends on the programmed delay. Capacity plots compare STM and product reconstruction capabilities for varying delays, and NRMSE plots compare performance against different reservoir types (TDQRC vs TDLRC) for forecasting tasks.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the physical setup and the concept of engineering memory via delayed feedback. It then uses capacity benchmarks (STM, product) to separate the roles of waveguide propagation (timing) and Kerr nonlinearity (feature transformation). Finally, it applies this framework to forecasting chaotic time series (Mackey-Glass) to compare model performance.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges quantum optics (waveguide QED, cavity QED) with quantum information processing (reservoir computing), providing a concrete physical platform for realizing complex quantum computation tasks.
